t: Nothing remains of Leicester House, a large aristocratic townhouse that stood north of what is now Leicester Square until it was demolished in 1791. The Earl of Leicester built it, and it was completed in 1635. Elizabeth Stuart, the Winter Queen of Bohemia, lived here. In the 1700s it was home to two successive Hanoverian princes of Wales. Frederick, Prince of Wales, died here, and several children of George II were born here, among them Prince William, the Duke of Cumberland, who is remembered for his part at Culloden.
